item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00033","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C15","C13","C16"],"selected_candidate_label":"C15","confidence":0.94,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C15 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both memoranda concern private tax legislation that would revive an untimely refund or tax claim, explain why limitations periods must remain effective, examine whether special equitable circumstances justify an exception, and reject relief because it would discriminate by singling out particular taxpayers. The child’s extended defense of limitations—especially the risks from lost records, unavailable witnesses, and difficult proof—closely parallels C15’s discussion of stale claims and lost evidence. C13 is also highly similar in its treatment of named taxpayers’ late filing and unfair discrimination against similarly situated taxpayers, but it lacks C15’s fuller limitations-policy framework. C16 has parallel general-law-versus-private-relief reasoning but concerns Social Security rather than tax administration.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Congress has determined it to be sound policy to include in the revenue system a statute of limitations... Such a provision is essential to finality in tax administration.","parent_excerpt":"Since the bill grants relief from the operation of the statute of limitation, special equitable circumstances should appear which require that this taxpayer be singled out for special relief.","explanation":"Both frame the private bill as an attempted exception to a tax limitation period and require a special equitable justification for departing from the general rule."},{"child_excerpt":"after the passing of a reasonable period of time, witnesses may have died, records may have been destroyed or lost, and problems of proof and administration of tax claims become too burdensome","parent_excerpt":"This unilateral statement... illustrates the desirability of a statute of limitations which disposes of stale claims and the necessity for retaining or securing evidence with respect thereto.","explanation":"The child expands C15’s distinctive administrative justification for limitations: stale tax claims become unreliable because evidence may no longer be available."},{"child_excerpt":"This bill, by singling out two of these taxpayers for special relief from the statute of limitations, would unjustly discriminate against other taxpayers similarly situated.","parent_excerpt":"the proposed legislation would be discriminatory and would single out a particular taxpayer for relief from the statute of limitations without adequate reason","explanation":"This is a close literal and functional match in the concluding rationale, adapted from one taxpayer to two taxpayers."}]}
